    What Lecture 1 settled

    Lecture 2

    What do I fill in at each stage, and where does the OTS feed it?

    Lecture 2 · the plan

    From raw data to a closed ledger

    1. Bring the OTS data inthree live pulls, or a CSV for standalone copies
    2. Engage and Definethe run / safe-park / shut-down call and a testable statement
    3. Explorefishbone, IS / IS NOT, hypotheses screened S / D / N
    4. Plantests ranked by V = I/C and the cost ledger
    5. Do it and Look backverdicts, the fix, and what stops it coming back

    Before any stage

    Pull the simulator's data in as evidence

    Every stage argues from data. The tab fetches it from the running OTS.

    Run data
    every DCS trend so far, 5 s steps
    CSV
    Snapshot
    every transmitter now vs design
    table
    Event log
    alarms, trips, operator actions
    list

    No live link?

    Standalone copies take a CSV instead

    1

    OTS ▸ Data export ▸ download the run, snapshot and log CSV.

    2

    Workbook ▸ OTS data & evidence ▸ drop the files on the box.

    3

    Give each dataset a role: initial run, test or after fix.

    Evidence is tagged

    Fact, inference or opinion?

    Each line of evidence carries a tag. TE-1 has all three kinds.

    Fact

    FIC-201 reads 0.00 m³/h with output 100 %.

    read from an instrument

    Inference

    V-201 lost ≈ 1.9 m³/h more than it received.

    worked out from facts

    Opinion

    "The new operator's step caused it."

    a claim, not yet tested

    Stage 1 · Engage

    First call: run, safe-park or shut down

    Rate safety, environment, equipment and production first.

    TE-1: pumps running without liquid → safe-park, then diagnose.

    Stage 2 · Define

    A problem statement a test can check

    Engage bought time. Define says exactly what is wrong.

    What: feed FI-201 Where: V-201 → P-201A/B → FV-201 How: 0.00 m³/h, valve wide open Norm: 60 m³/h When: lost at −00:02:28

    Stage 3 · Explore

    Fishbone and IS / IS NOT narrow the field

    • Put every candidate cause on one of the six branches.
    • IS / IS NOT: where the fault is, and where it could be but is not.

    Stage 3 · Explore

    Write each cause as “if … then we should observe …”

    Cause
    the mechanism, on one fishbone branch
    WH-n
    If … then
    what the plant must show if it is true
    prediction
    Key
    the reading that tells it apart
    tag
    Falsifier
    the observation that would kill it
    tag
    WH-1: if V-201 ran down, LG-201 reads low and both pumps give no head.

    Interactive — click the cells

    Screen hypotheses against evidence: S / D / N

    S
    evidence supports it
    D
    evidence denies it → killed
    N
    neutral

    One solid D kills a hypothesis; a pile of S never proves one — only a test can confirm.

    Interactive — drag the sliders

    Rank the survivors: P × S × T

    $$\text{Tier 1: } S=5 \text{ or } P\,S\,T\ge 48 \qquad \text{Tier 2: } P\,S\,T\ge 18$$

    P, S, T: scores 1 (low) to 5 (high), set by the team.

    The scores only order the work — saying P, S and T aloud is what makes the team agree what to test first.

    Stage 4 · Plan

    Each test: one move, one reading, a prediction per hypothesis

    Tier 1 hypotheses now need tests that tell them apart.

    $n$
    hypotheses the test targets
    –
    $m$
    largest group predicting the same direction
    –
    $I$
    information: $\log_2(n/m)$
    bit
    $C$
    cost of the test
    USD
    $V$
    $I$ per USD 1 000
    bit/kUSD

    Interactive — change a cost

    Order TE-1's tests: cheap first, then highest V

    From the previous slide$I=\log_2\dfrac{n}{m}\qquad V=\dfrac{I}{C/1000}$

    Free observations go first; among paid tests the one that splits the hypotheses for the least money comes next, and the plant change comes last.

    Stage 4 → Stage 6

    The cost ledger: opened in Plan, closed in Look back

    TE-1 itemKindUSD
    Tests T-1 to T-5diagnosis1 200
    Lost margin, 0.75 h × 5 809 USD/hsafe-park4 360
    Prime P-201B (assumed)fix, now500
    Rev B: LT-201 alarms on DCS (assumed)fix, permanent3 000
    Total9 060

    Stage 5 · Do it

    Run the tests on the OTS, then write the verdicts

    The plan named a move and a reading. Do it records what happened.

    • Pull the test's run data as a test dataset.
    • Mark each hypothesis: consistent or killed.
    • Confirmed cause → the mechanism in 5.1.

    Stage 6 · Look back

    Make it stay fixed

    • Barriers with owners: alarm, procedure, training.
    • Close the ledger against the target.
    • Two lessons: do again, never do.

    Lecture 2 · summary

    What Lecture 2 settled

    • Evidence comes from the OTS: live pull or CSV.
    • Hypotheses are “if … then”, screened S / D / N.
    • Rank by P×S×T; order tests by cost, then V = I/C.
    • The ledger opens in Plan and closes in Look back.

    Lecture 3

    How does a finished case look, and how do I hand mine in?

    Lecture 3 · the plan

    One finished case, then your own

    1. Open TE-1 from Worked examplesit never loads by itself
    2. Replay the evidencewhy the history before the call decides the case
    3. Report and team slideswhat the workbook writes for you
    4. Save, open, hand inone .woods.json per team, checked stage by stage

    Worked examples

    Load TE-1 on purpose

    Open example loads every stage filled; Download gives the .woods.json.

    TE-1 is a worked case for everyone, not a graded exercise.

    TE-1 · The temperatures go crazy

    What you are told when you are called

    First start-up of a new unit; it has run well for several shifts. About an hour ago the new operator raised the column pressure set point by 0.1 MPa. About 20 minutes later the tray temperatures began to swing; now the bottoms level is falling. It is cold (−1 °C).

    Interactive — drag through time

    Replay TE-1 from 49 minutes before the call

    The feed held for 16 min after the pressure step and only then fell — the swings follow the feed loss, not the step.

    TE-1 · worked answer

    Symptom, cause, remedy

    The replay pointed at the feed path. Tests T-1 to T-5 confirmed WH-1.

    SymptomFeed 0 m³/h, FV-201 wide open, trays swinging, sump falling
    CauseV-201 ran down (57 in, 60 out); both feed pumps gas-bound
    RemedySafe-park, prime P-201A, FIC-201 to AUTO; rev B level alarms

    Outputs

    The workbook writes the report and the team slides

    • Report: Word-style, stage by stage, with your figures.
    • Slides: one deck for the team presentation.
    • The readiness check lists any empty MUST step.

    Interactive — tick what your team has

    Ready to hand in?

    Hand in one .woods.json per team plus the report — File ▸ Open on any copy restores every stage.

    Class Activity

    Can you solve it yourself?

    Class Activity · the plan

    Three problems on TE-1's evidence

    1. Problem 1 · tag the evidencefact, inference or opinion (Lecture 2)
    2. Problem 2 · screen three hypothesesS / D / N and who survives (Lecture 2)
    3. Problem 3 · order the testsI, V = I/C and the run order (Lecture 2)

    Problem 1.1 · statement · read first

    PROBLEM 1.1Fact, inference or opinion?

    Tag each line from the TE-1 notebook as Fact, Inference or Opinion, and give the reason in a few words.

    1. PIC-210 1.494 and the independent PI-211 1.494 MPa g agree.
    2. V-201 from 64 % to 40 % in 4 h means about 1.9 m³/h more out than in.
    3. "It must be the pressure step — it was the last thing anyone changed."
    4. Feed preheat TIC-202 is 145.7 °C because no feed flows through E-201.
    5. Upstream unit by phone: "We are sending 57 m³/h to V-201."

    Problem 1.1 · solution

    PROBLEM 1.1Tags and reasons

    #TagReason
    1Facttwo instruments read
    2Inferencecomputed from the rounds log
    3Opiniona claim, untested
    4Inferencereading plus a "because"
    5Facta first-hand report, recorded

    Problem 1.2 · statement · read first

    PROBLEM 1.2Screen three hypotheses

    Mark each evidence line S, D or N against each hypothesis, then say which survive.

    HypothesisPredicts
    WH-3 PIC-210 reads wrongPI-211 and PG-211 disagree with PIC-210
    WH-4 FV-201 / FT-201 failedpumps quiet, high head, V-201 level normal
    WH-6 feed line frozenpumps dead-headed, high head, V-201 rising
    • Ev-6 PIC-210, PI-211 and PG-211 all read 1.49 MPa g.
    • Ev-9 P-201A rattling, PG-203A 453 kPa g: no head.
    • Ev-10 LG-201 ≈ 25 %, falling over the rounds.

    Problem 1.2 · solution

    PROBLEM 1.2All three are killed

    Ev-6Ev-9Ev-10Verdict
    WH-3DNNkilled
    WH-4NDDkilled
    WH-6NDDkilled

    One D is enough; no head plus a low drum points back to supply.

    Problem 1.3 · statement · read first

    PROBLEM 1.3Order the five tests

    For each test find $n$, $m$, $I$ and $V$, then give the run order: free first, then highest $V$, the plant change last.

    TestPredictions of its targetsUSD
    T-1 compare pressure gaugesWH-3 ↑, WH-1 =0
    T-2 trend reviewWH-1 ↓, WH-2 =, WH-5 =0
    T-3 field look at pumps, LG-201WH-1 ↓, WH-4 =, WH-6 =100
    T-4 phone upstreamWH-1 ↓, WH-2 ↑100
    T-5 prime and start P-201AWH-1 ↑, WH-4 =1 000

    Problem 1.3 · solution

    PROBLEM 1.3T-1, T-2, then T-4, T-3, and T-5 last

    From Lecture 2$I=\log_2\dfrac{n}{m}\qquad V=\dfrac{I}{C/1000}$
    $I_{T4}=\log_2\tfrac{2}{1}=1,\;V_{T4}=\tfrac{1}{0.1}=10$opposite predictions: m = 1
    $I_{T3}=\log_2\tfrac{3}{2}=0.58,\;V_{T3}=5.8$two of three predict "="
    $I_{T5}=1,\;V_{T5}=\tfrac{1}{1.0}=1.0$plant change: last anyway

    T-1 and T-2 are free: run them first.

    Take home

    Key Takeaways

    1

    Work in the tab when the OTS runs; take a CSV everywhere else.

    2

    Write every cause as “if … then”, and let one D kill it.

    3

    Run free tests first, then the highest V = I/C; plant changes last.

    4

    Read the history before the call before blaming the last change.
